title: Ratio and proportion you will actually use
hook: A transformer wound 10 : 1 has 230 V on its primary. How many volts come out of the secondary, and why does the current go up ten times instead of down?
oneBreath: A ratio like 3 : 2 compares two amounts by multiplying, not by taking one from the other: three of one for every two of the other, in that order and in the same units. Multiply or divide both parts by the same number and the ratio stays the same, so 3 : 2 is also 6 : 4 and 30 : 20, but adding the same number to both parts changes it. To share an amount in a ratio, add the parts to count the blocks, find what one block is worth, then build each share from it. A unit rate is an amount per one of something, such as grams of fuel per kWh, and it lets you scale to any amount for as long as the rate holds steady. Two amounts are in direct proportion when doubling one doubles the other, as a transformer's output voltage follows its input, while a fixed charge plus a rate rises steadily but is not in proportion. In inverse proportion one goes up as the other comes down and their product stays fixed, so halving a gas's volume doubles its absolute pressure, and a transformer that steps voltage down 10 : 1 steps current up ten times.

ideas.title: Ratios as blocks
ideas.oneLine: 3 : 2 means three of one for every two of the other, and the order matters: 10 : 1 is not 1 : 10.

ideas.title: Equivalent ratios and scaling
ideas.oneLine: Multiply or divide both parts by the same number to keep a ratio, since adding the same number to both breaks it.

ideas.title: Sharing in a ratio
ideas.oneLine: Add the parts to count the blocks, find one block, then each share: 40 litres in 3 : 2 is 24 and 16.

ideas.title: Unit rates
ideas.oneLine: Turn a rate into an amount per one (per hour, per kWh, per turn) and scale from it, but only where the rate holds steady.

ideas.title: Direct proportion
ideas.oneLine: Two amounts are in direct proportion when doubling one doubles the other, like a transformer's output voltage, and a fixed charge plus a rate is not.

ideas.title: Inverse proportion
ideas.oneLine: One goes up as the other comes down with their product fixed: halve a gas's volume and its absolute pressure doubles.

calibration.q: A mix is 2 : 3. You use 6 parts of the first. How many parts of the second keep the same mix?
calibration.why: 6 is 2 × 3, so the second part is times 3 too: 3 × 3 = 9. 7 adds 4 to both parts, which changes the mix, and 4 reads the ratio the wrong way round.

calibration.q: A gas fills 6 litres at 100 kPa absolute. Kept at the same temperature, it is squeezed into 3 litres. What is its absolute pressure now?
calibration.why: Pressure × volume stays the same: 100 × 6 = 600, and 600 ÷ 3 = 200 kPa, so halving the volume doubles the pressure. 50 kPa treats it as direct, and 103 kPa adds the 3 litres taken away.
